subject.declared_domain: The boundary between the C0 rung (facts / nodes) and the C1 rung (interactions / edges), as D1's edge_grain_binding names it: HAS_FIELD, described there as 'structural field membership (the C0/C1 boundary)'. This card covers that BOUNDARY CLAIM -- what it asserts, where it is stated, how much of the estate it accounts for, and how it fails. It does NOT card the C0 or C1 rungs themselves (0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X's SC-a-*/SC-b-*), nor the D1 rail (wave 1, SC-e-*).

methodology.how: ⛔ THE BOUNDARY IS A PARENTHETICAL, NOT A STRUCTURE -- and that is the substance of this subject. It exists as five words inside one value string in D1's edge_grain_binding: HAS_FIELD is bound at field grain with the gloss 'structural field membership (the C0/C1 boundary)'. There is no boundary object, no boundary field, no predicate a consumer can evaluate, and nothing in the graph marks an edge as boundary-crossing. The claim COMPOSES the HAS_FIELD edge type and the C0/C1 rung vocabulary; it INVENTS the designation itself -- the assertion that this one edge type is where facts become interactions. Nothing computes it and nothing checks it.

declared_opinions: ⛔ THE DEFINITE ARTICLE: the gloss says 'THE C0/C1 boundary', asserting singularity. Whether one edge type can be the whole boundary between two rungs is a declared position, not a derived one, and the relations vocabulary in the same file does not support it (see coverage).

STRUCTURAL MEMBERSHIP AS THE CRITERION: the boundary is drawn at 'structural field membership' -- an edge that says a thing HAS a field, rather than an edge that moves a value. That is a choice about what makes a rung transition, and it excludes flow edges by construction.

THE BOUNDARY IS AN ANNOTATION, NOT A TYPE: it lives in prose beside a grain binding rather than in any field. No consumer can branch on it, and this is knowingly the same F-2 shape the wave has been routing all evening -- recorded here rather than fixed, per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX.

Its containing block parsed with yaml.safe_load. materializer_standing is MEASURED as not_applicable: the designation is a hand-authored gloss with no producer, so no materializer's currency is in question. ⛔ THE 'PARENTHETICAL NOT A STRUCTURE' CLAIM IS MEASURED RATHER THAN RHETORICAL: I searched the graph schema for any boundary marker and there is none -- CALL table_info('CloudEdge') returns exactly four properties (edge_type, layer, snapshot_ts, props) and none of them encodes rung or boundary. So the boundary genuinely has nowhere to live except this string.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: NOTHING, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING TO ASK. The designation is prose inside another field's value: no consumer can query whether an edge crosses the C0/C1 boundary, so the failure is not a wrong answer but the absence of an askable question. A consumer wanting boundary-crossing edges must hardcode HAS_FIELD -- and will then silently exclude every sibling.
silent_degrade_paths: a consumer hardcoding HAS_FIELD as the boundary gets 4,269 edges and silently excludes HAS_PROP's 359, which carry the same structural-membership shape over D1's other declared field-grain atom

the designation lives inside a value string, so a parser reading edge_grain_binding structurally gets the grain and drops the boundary claim entirely -- it is invisible to any consumer that does not read prose
the same file makes a second, unreconciled statement about HAS_FIELD at :141 (one of nine containment edges); a consumer reading either location alone gets a coherent and incomplete picture
the embedded 4269 currently agrees with live, so a consumer citing it is right today and has no marker telling them it is a 34-day-old stamp that could drift like its siblings did

ARM 1 (the silent exclusion): counted the nine contains-family members and confirmed HAS_PROP returns 359 edges -- a real, non-empty population that a HAS_FIELD-only boundary query excludes without any signal. ARM 2 (POSITIVE CONTROL, same query shape on the named type): HAS_FIELD -> 4,269, matching the declared value exactly. verdict.why: The designation is stated in exactly one place, its edge type resolves cleanly against the live graph, and its embedded count still holds exactly at 4,269 -- the only count in its block that does. As a pointer to where the ontology cuts C0 from C1 it works. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three bounded defects: (1) it asserts singularity with a definite article that the file's own relations vocabulary contradicts -- HAS_FIELD is one of nine containment edges, and its nearest structural sibling HAS_PROP carries the identical one-edge-per-atom shape over Prop, D1's OTHER declared field-grain atom; (2) the boundary is a parenthetical inside another field's value, so it is invisible to any structural parser and unqueryable by any consumer, which is knowingly the F-2 shape; (3) the same file makes a second unreconciled statement about the same edge type, and a reader of either location alone gets a coherent partial picture. Not UNSOUND: nothing here shows the cut is in the wrong place, and I explicitly do not claim HAS_PROP should be the boundary -- that judgement belongs to the ontology's owner. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked and every scalar is 'measured', the second card in my set where the subject was fully reachable. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION per W2-m-3: omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on this designation's future.
